subject: computer-science
title: Internet & WWW: How Web Pages Load
welcome_lead: Every page is the result of a tiny conversation between your browser and a server.
meta_desc: KS3 web: request-response cycle, HTML, CSS, JavaScript intro.
final_note: Three languages build almost every site you've ever used.

concepts.def: Language used to structure web pages.
Style sheet language for colours and layout.
Language that makes web pages interactive.
A browser asking a server for a page.
Computer that stores and sends web pages.

walkthroughs.body_html: Your browser sends an HTTP request. The web server sends a response with the HTML page. Your browser draws it.
HTML is the bones (headings, paragraphs). CSS is the clothes (colour, layout). JavaScript is the brain (clicks, animations).
Browsers cache (save) files so the next visit loads quicker. Servers spread the load across many machines so popular sites don't crash.

mcqs.q: Why are passwords stored as hashes rather than plaintext?
options: Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Hashes are encryption that can be decrypted with the right key.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
Hashes are one-way - even an attacker who steals them cannot easily recover passwords.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Because TCP cannot handle video data.
Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
O(1) - because it is fast.
